electricity.title: How Much U.S. Data Center Electricity Is Renewable or Carbon-Free?
electricity.explanation: On the physical U.S. power grids where data centers sit, ~44% of generation is carbon-free (~24% renewables + ~20% nuclear) and ~56% comes from fossil fuels (LBNL / IEA / EPA eGRID). Separately, hyperscalers (Google, Meta, Microsoft, AWS) match 100% of annual MWh via wind/solar Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs) and RECs—financing clean generation nationwide even when local grids burn gas at night.
electricity.source: LBNL 2024 Report, EPA eGRID & Corporate Sustainability Audits

water.title: How Much Data Center Cooling Water Is Recycled / Non-Potable?
water.explanation: Unlike electricity, water cannot be generated via certificates—it is strictly local. Nationally, less than 5% of U.S. data center cooling water comes from recycled municipal wastewater ('purple pipe' greywater), while >95% draws from potable municipal systems, rivers, or aquifers (LBNL / S&P Global). However, next-generation AI campuses (e.g., Stargate Abilene, Microsoft Fairwater) increasingly adopt closed-loop liquid cooling to eliminate continuous evaporative water loss.
water.source: LBNL 2024 Report, USGS & Municipal Utility Filings

energy.subtitle: Annual U.S. electricity consumption across major economic sectors and energy-intensive industries
energy.takeaway: U.S. data centers consumed 176 TWh in 2023 (4.4% of all U.S. electricity)—larger than several heavy manufacturing subsectors, and projected by Lawrence Berkeley National Lab to reach 325–580 TWh (6.7%–12%) by 2028 due to AI.

water.dcShareSub: of U.S. sector water (17.4B gal direct cooling)
water.dcProjectionCallout: ~44× less than U.S. golf courses · +211B gal indirect at power plants
water.subtitle: Annual U.S. water consumption & withdrawals — comparing direct cooling vs. major water users
water.takeaway: Nationally, U.S. data centers directly consume ~17.4 billion gallons/year (~45x less than U.S. golf courses and >2,000x less than farm irrigation). However, local impacts can be acute: a single evaporative hyperscale campus in a drought-prone county can consume 20–30% of a small city's water supply, and indirect power-plant cooling adds ~211B gallons/year.
water.distinctionNote: Withdrawals = total water diverted from rivers/aquifers (much of thermoelectric power water is returned downstream). Consumption = water evaporated or absorbed and not immediately returned locally.

land.dcProjectionCallout: 16× less land than U.S. golf courses — though single AI campuses now span 1,000–3,200 acres
land.subtitle: Physical U.S. land footprint — comparing data center campuses against agriculture, cities, and recreation
land.takeaway: Nationally, all U.S. data centers combined occupy roughly 0.005% of U.S. land (~100,000–150,000 acres—less than 1/10th the land covered by U.S. golf courses). Locally, however, new 1,000–3,000+ acre AI campuses increasingly convert rural farmland near high-voltage transmission corridors.
